News.title: This is not a drill: Germany lose a World Cup penalty shoot-out
News.content:
“I do not have much to say. This is now my second World Cup and we have missed moving onto the next round twice now in a row. I want to apologise for that. We are all very disappointed. We had many plans for this year’s World Cup. It is not a very good feeling to disappoint again. The team tried a lot. One goal was disallowed. We had a very strong opponent; it was difficult to create chances and keep the pace. The Paraguayan team defended very deep and it was difficult to run for a long time. We tried to move over the flanks but unfortunately, it did not really work out. I do not think we deserved to win this time.

“I do not think we allowed many chances. We were on the ball, in the momentum, especially after the equaliser. We ended up in the shoot-out. It was not easy because I missed that penalty kick and it is a 50/50 chance. During the tournament, you really have to give it your all. I do not think we played bad football, but something was always missing and that was the case today as well. As players, we need to look at ourselves and what we can do better. We play for such a big football nation. If you get eliminated early, you do not deserve to stay.”

News.title: Djokovic revels in role of pantomime villain... and earns wedding invite
News.content:
Has anyone in sport ever revelled with quite such gusto as Novak Djokovic at feeling like the world is against them? At one set all here, the Wimbledon crowd had, in the words of John McEnroe, turned very vocally from thinking “who?” to chants of “Wuuuu” in support of the Chinese underdog Wu Yibing.

The world No 99 had not just quietly got himself back into the match after losing the first set, but was actually beginning to dictate with his rasping forehand as the players traded games to 4-4 in the third.

Djokovic took exception previously to the Wimbledon crowd supporting Holger Rune against him and, with just about every losing point here prompting an ever louder cry of “Wuuuu”, the 39-year-old seven-time champion looked suddenly both irritated and energised.

A sensational passing shot interspersed with some brilliantly dogged hitting from the back of the court clinched a crucial third-set service break, with Djokovic then celebrating not with a clenched fist but by pointedly holding a prolonged finger to his ear.

Djokovic’s son, Stefan, was also off his feet with a huge fist pump before his father fought off a series of break points to hold serve and move two sets to one ahead with a defiant arm to the sky.

News.title: Gabriel Martinelli the unlikely saviour after Japan make Brazil look average
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Brazil vs Japan in the 2026 World Cup round of 32.

The two sides meet at Houston Stadium with temperatures are expected to be in the mid-thirties, which should favour Carlo Ancelotti’s men over their Japanese opponents, but there is plenty of intrigue for the match ahead this evening.

Brazil have no suspensions to worry about, but there are two key questions for fitness. Raphinha is expected to miss the match with a hamstring problem, and he could be a longer-term absence if they manage to get through to the next round.

Another question hangs over Santos, with the 34-year-old still yet to prove his full fitness, while Rayan, Matheus Cunha and Vinicius Jr. have done little wrong so far. A draw against Morocco was followed by wins against Haiti and Scotland to give them top spot in Group C, but it’s fair to say they have not truly been tested so far.

Japan have their own injury over Takefusa Kubo, who has a knee problem from the 2-2 draw with the Netherlands. The side drew 1-1 with Sweden, but managed to defeat Tunisia 4-0. Like Brazil, they are yet to really dominate a quality side, so they also have something to prove.

Right now, France lead Argentina as favourites to win the tournament, but Brazil are alongside Spain, England and Germany as the next sides most likely to secure glory. A confident win over Japan might start to change minds and build momentum.

Japan should not be overawed, though. They defeated Brazil 3-2 last year in October in Tokyo, coming from behind for a famous win.

The winner here will face the victor of tomorrow’s match between Ivory Coast and Norway.

News.title: Norrie’s silver lining to first-round exit... he can now attend own stag do
News.content:
Given his pedigree as a fierce grass-court competitor, few would have predicted Cameron Norrie to fall in the opening round at Wimbledon for the first time in eight years.

But as the only seeded British player at this year’s Championships walked off court after his arm-wrestle of a match against American Michael Zheng, a qualifier ranked 115 places below him, even he might be able to see one small silver lining. Norrie will at least be free to attend his own stag do in Ibiza the weekend after next.

Norrie was a quarter-finalist here last year and reached the semi-finals in 2022, so a deep run at this year’s tournament might have resulted in a scheduling mishap. But he can breathe easy after suffering a 6-7, 6-2, 6-7, 6-3, 7-6 defeat by the world No 144, which will at least free him up for the big bash on Wimbledon finals weekend.

“It always stinks to lose, especially at Wimbledon, my favourite tournament in the world, a tournament I always play so well at,” said Norrie, who will marry his American fiancée Louise Jacobi in December. “There’s no hiding from it. Yeah, it stinks. Especially tomorrow, everyone is still in the tournament, and you’re out. You’re just wanting to play. So it’s tough.”

News.title: UAE-backed Sudan rebels ‘training in Libya’
News.content:
Sudanese rebel fighters are being trained to use drones, heavy machine guns and rocket launchers in a network of secret camps in Libya, investigators have claimed.

Lighthouse Reports, a Dutch non-profit media organisation, alleged that southern Libya has become a key hub for training and supplying the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group that has been repeatedly accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s civil war.

Drawing on interviews with RSF defectors and Libyan National Army (LNA) officers, and open source analysis, the investigators detail how Sudanese fighters receive training from UAE-backed Colombian mercenaries and Libyan soldiers.

The video investigation, which was produced in conjunction with Sudan War Monitor, a group of journalists and open-source researchers, and Evident Media, a non-profit visual investigation organisation, is the latest contribution to a growing body of evidence that the conflict in Sudan has evolved into a regional proxy war.

Earlier this year, Reuters reported that thousands of RSF fighters had undergone training in a secret camp in Ethiopia. The UAE has long been widely accused of backing the RSF – allegations it has repeatedly denied.

News.title: Ben Stokes is gone and he leaves behind a broken England team
News.content:
Like many people I was dumbfounded yesterday when the whispers started coming out that Ben Stokes was about to announce his retirement. It was both shocking and perhaps inevitable at the same time. This is a guy that has given everything to the England shirt but also has worn his emotions on his sleeve throughout that journey. The truth is that the job just burns you out, especially if you take on as much responsibility as Ben did in the role. He will rightly go down as one of England’s genuine greats, and I would go as far as saying he played the two greatest Test innings I have ever seen at Headingley in 2019 and at Lords in 2023.

His innings in the 2019 World Cup final would also be up there with the very best in that format too. This is a guy who revelled in the big moments. A genuine superstar. It doesn’t feel like a time for negatives and so I hesitate to say this but I’m not convinced that the whole thing was orchestrated the right way yesterday - it seems like a huge distraction to a team that was battling to avoid a series defeat and the the cricket in the last session very much had an ‘end of term’ feel to it. Everyone has the right to bow out on their own terms, and no-one has earned that more than Ben, but announcing before or after the game seems like a more sensible approach.

When you are in the middle of a match, the only thing that matters is the performance of the team. It is a small gripe in the greater scheme of things. English cricket will be far worse (and less interesting!) without Ben involved. Opposition teams will be breathing a sigh of relief and there will be a huge vacuum in the England team that will be impossible to fill.

Sports.title: Why England need Declan Rice AND Elliot Anderson vs DR Congo – but World Cup hopes could be ended by Premier League star
Sports.content:
ENGLAND face DR Congo in the Round of 32 at the World Cup, hoping to avoid the same fate as Germany.

The Three Lions’ old rivals were stunned by a penalty shootout defeat to Paraguay, but England’s German manager Thomas Tuchel will be looking for his side to finally hit their stride after flat performances against Ghana and Panama.





Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham helped get the job done in the 2-0 win over Panama to secure England‘s passage as top dog in Group L, which booked a date against DR Congo in the Round of 32.

Struggles against sides playing a low block have been clear to see, with the African nation expected to set up in a similar fashion.

That means England will have a tactical conundrum to solve once again.

And to help us to understand how Tuchel and his staff might look to leap past The Leopards, SunSport’s tactics guru Dean Scoggins returns for the latest episode of Team Talk.



Rice v Anderson

There has been an interesting debate about who should play out of Elliot Anderson or Declan Rice. Elliot Anderson played solo in midfield against Panama, putting on a passing clinic against the Canal Men.

Bellingham was paired with the Nottingham Forest man for that clash rather than another traditional centre-mid, with the Real Madrid star coming up trumps with a goal and assist.

But according to Kyle Walker, who has joined SunSport as a special World Cup analyst, he believes England should look to get more from their full-backs by playing £116million Anderson alongside £105m Rice.

Walker believes the pair would help to neutralise the counter-attacking threat posed by DR Congo, with full-backs Nico O’Reilly and Djed Spence then able to bomb on to support the wingers.

DR Congo are set to play in a narrow 5-3-2 shape, rather than with wingers. And they are not to be underestimated given they were able to earn a draw against European powerhouse Portugal.

That means England’s 3-1-6 attacking shape could be susceptible to turning over possession with Anderson isolated 2v1 in the middle of the park.

However, playing Rice alongside Anderson would eliminate such an overload, while O’Reilly and Spence can invert to create numerical superiority infield.

We have previously spoken about England’s triangle’s as well, and having the sitting pair of Rice and Anderson would give the full-backs the chance to create those overloads out wide.



Stones at right back?

England are running a bit short at full-back this tournament – a sentence you would have been considered crazy for saying two years ago.

In Walker’s day, he says it was a struggle to get a place. But with Reece James carrying a knock and Jarrell Quansah hobbling off against Panama, Spence has been left as the only natural option to play there.

However, Burnley defender Walker has suggested John Stones might be able to play there. But he looked sluggish at centre-back in the opener against Croatia.

The argument could be to also play Ezri Konsa there and set up with three centre-backs when in possession, but the concern with that is leaving the right winger alone to provide the width and pace when defending transitions.



DR Congo have dangerous runners on the counter-attack, meaning England should set up in more of a 2-2-6 or 2-4-4.

With Stones, that doesn’t work. He simply does not have the pace to recover if he is caught out of possession. Spence however would have the pace to cover even if he was asked to sit in build up.

The Wissa threat

Yoane Wissa might not have had the best of seasons for Newcastle in the Premier League, but at the World Cup he has looked very sharp as one of the two strikers up front for his country.

DR Congo’s 5-3-2 shape leaves two threats up front, which leaves Tuchel with the headache of having a 3v2.



Wissa plays in a semi-circle behind his striker partner, which worked great against Uzbekistan as he nipped in on a heavy touch to win a penalty and then score from the spot.

There is also the threat from the wing-backs when DR Congo do attack. Premier League fans will be quite familiar with the sight of Arthur Masuaku and Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

The likes of Axel Tuanzebe, Noah Sadiki and Chancel Mbemba will also be credible threats.

This game is certainly no given, and England can’t afford any complacency against an opponent who will keep them honest.

Sports.title: Awkward moment Brazil fan accidentally destroys pub TV with giant cardboard CANARY while celebrating World Cup winner
Sports.content:
A BRAZIL fan’s World Cup celebration went horribly wrong when he destroyed a TV… with a giant CANARY.

There were wild scenes at one streetside bar when Gabriel Martinelli scored a last-gasp winner against Japan on Monday.





The Samurai Blue were on course to pull off a huge upset until Casemiro and Martinelli completed the Selecao’s second-half turnaround in a 2-1 victory.

And Brazil supporters had to wait until the 96th minute for the Arsenal winger to save the day.

But the moment was ruined for one punter, who is sure to be handed a whopping bill after obliterating a huge flat-screen TV.

It all went pear-shaped when he picked up a giant cardboard cut-out of a canary wearing a Brazil strip.

By lifting it off the ground, the canary’s arm pushed the screen off its wall mount and it tumbled to the ground.

Ploughing into two wooden tables on its way to the floor, the TV lay face-down but there is little doubt its display was smashed to pieces.

The crowd watched on in a mixture of shock and jubilation – still buzzing with the winner Martinelli netted seconds prior.

The clip was viewed hundreds of thousands of times on X, where one user commented: “You’re going to have to buy another TV.”

Sports.title: Footballer Maddy Cusack’s coach branded her ‘psycho’ and commented on her weight before she was found dead, inquest told
Sports.content:
FOOTBALLER Maddy Cusack’s coach branded her a “psycho” and commented on her weight before she was found dead, an inquest heard.

Jonathan Morgan also allegedly played mind games with the star, 27, after he joined Sheffield United.





Maddy was discovered hanged at her home address in Horsley, Derbyshire, on September 20, 2023.

Chesterfield Coroner’s Court heard Morgan had previously been Maddy’s manager at Leicester City.

She was said to have been “so happy” to leave the club as he reportedly made life “unpleasant” for her.

The inquest heard she was “loving life” until he became her coach again at Sheffield United in February 2023.



Maddy’s partner Grace Riglar, who played for the club at the same time as her, said the player was “anxious” about Morgan joining.

She said: “I think it was stuff she told me about her previous experience prior to Jonathan coming to Sheffield.

“I think she said that they played a game against a team while Jonathan was the manager. She had done something on the pitch and Jonathan called her a psycho from the sideline.

“I don’t think she let anyone know those types of comments affected her but they did and they made her uncomfortable.”



She said Morgan joining United was a big cause of Maddy’s stress, which coincided with her being unhappy there.

Grace also claimed Maddy thought the coach made a “personal attack” on her by not putting her in the starting line-up for matches.

She told the court: “She was used to starting every game, she was an important member of the team. When Jonathan came, she was in and out from the starting team a bit.



“Her going from starting to being on the bench quite a lot, she saw that as a setback. That impacted her a lot.

“I just think she almost felt like it was a bit of a personal attack and that Jonathan was playing mind games with her by starting her one week and dropping her the next.

“She just felt those little things were intentional.”

Grace said Morgan made comments about their relationship and claimed he called her “Mrs Cusack”.

When Morgan joined United, he reportedly told the players in the first meeting that if anyone was in a relationship within the team, they had to tell him.



Grace continued: “She found it uncomfortable when Jonathan would call me ‘Mrs Cusack’, especially in front of other players.

“We wanted to keep our relationship very professional. The football side and relationship side were very separate.”

She also accused the coach of remarking on Maddy’s weight – causing the footballer to change her eating and exercise habits.

This included not eating carbohydrates, skipping breakfast and going for extra runs after training – despite being “one of the fittest players on the team”, Grace said.

She also claimed Maddy told her before she died that she wanted to move to Dubai and be a flight attendant.



Grace added: “She didn’t want to go back to playing football. I don’t think she really knew how to get out of that situation.”

Maddy’s dad David Cusack yesterday told how Morgan was in the “firing line” following his daughter’s death.

He also claimed his daughter “never came across a character” like Morgan before, including the “way he dealt with people”.

Speaking about him joining Sheffield Utd, he added: “(She was) dismayed by the possibility of him coming back into her life. I’m going to say ‘look, it may have changed. It’s a fresh start for both of you’. I tried to be positive.”

Sports.title: Newcastle star Yoane Wissa and DR Congo ORDERED to dump England out of World Cup by country’s PRESIDENT
Sports.content:
YOANE WISSA and his DR Congo teammates have been ordered to beat England – by presidential decree.

The Leopards are due to face Thomas Tuchel‘s men in Atlanta tomorrow, where they will be huge underdogs





The central African nation last competed at a World Cup in 1974, when they were still known as Zaire.

But they earned their Round of 32 place thanks to a 3-1 win over Uzbekistan, with Newcastle ace Wissa scoring twice.

Congolese president Felix Tshisekedi has now urged Sebastien Desabre’s side to shock the Three Lions and help unite the trouble-torn country.

Tshisekedi, 63, addressed the nation wearing a DR Congo team shirt.



He told the players: “Take the field against England with the calmness of people who have already honoured their country.

Sports.title: How DR Congo’s Gael Kakuta, 35, turned life around from snus addiction and Chelsea transfer ban to England World Cup tie
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE stars past and present have made history for DR Congo by securing a last 32 clash with England.

But one member of the squad is better known for off-the-field intrigue than anything he achieved on the pitch in English football.





Gael Kakuta is now 35 and spent the second half of last season at his FOURTEENTH club, Cypriot side AE Limassol.

Back in 2007, though, Kakuta was one of the hottest properties in world football.

And Chelsea seemed to have pulled off a big transfer coup when they pounced to sign the then-16-year-old from Lens.

Attacking midfielder Kakuta initially flourished in the club’s academy, with Didier Drogba taking the youngster under his wing when he trained with the first-team.

But just days after being promoted to Carlo Ancelotti’s senior squad in September 2009, Kakuta became famous for all the wrong reasons.

Lens had complained to Fifa about Chelsea inducing him to break his contract with them.

The world governing body’s Dispute Resolution Chamber sided with the French club and came down hard on Chelsea and Kakuta.

The teenager was suspended from playing for four months and ordered to pay Lens nearly £675,000.





The Blues were banned from signing players for the next two transfer windows and told to cough up £110,000 in compensation to the French club for Kakuta.

But Chelsea appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and won. The February 2010 ruling said Kakuta’s contract with Lens was invalid and his ban was lifted.

The Premier League club was also permitted to resume international transfers.

Meanwhile, Kakuta had made his first-team debut in November 2009 and weeks later became the youngest player to represent Chelsea in the Champions League.

In December 2010, he signed a new four-and-a-half-year contract but expressed a desire to gain first-team experience elsewhere.

Kakuta then joined the massed ranks of young Chelsea players out on loan.

He had temporary spells at Fulham, Bolton, Dijon, Vitesse Arnhem, Lazio and Rayo Vallecano between 2011 and 2015.

But the biggest headlines he made were in 2014 when a fraudster named Medi Abalimba was jailed for four years after posing as Kakuta and spending thousands of pounds on stolen credit cards.



While Kakuta was at Vallecano, he gave an interview in which he remained bullish about living up to his early promise.

Kakuta told The Independent: “From the first story from Lens, with the transfer ban and my ban also, people have heard my name since I was 17 so they’ve been expecting a lot from me since then.

“Things didn’t go the way people wanted so now they think I’m finished but I’m only 23 years old.

“Some players only really get their career going when they’re 28 so, for me, I have plenty of time and I will end up being where I should be.”

But it never really happened.

Kakuta’s Blues career, consisting of just 16 first-team appearances, ended when he joined Sevilla in 2015 for an undisclosed compensation fee – because he was still under 24.

He had spells in China and Spain before returning to France.

Probably the best spell of Kakuta’s club career came when he was back at Lens, initially on loan.



He had such a good season in Ligue 1 in 2020/21 that he won the Marc-Vivien Foe award for the best African player in the French top flight.

But a number of personal issues affected Kakuta’s ability to shine on the pitch.

He suffered from depression and took the oral tobacco known as “snus” to cope.

Kakuta’s father died when he was seven and he subsequently lost his younger sister and then his mother.

After his mum passed away, Kakuta found religion while playing in Iran.

He started last season in Turkey’s second tier and then moved to Limassol in February, scoring once in seven appearances.

Kakuta, who was born in Lille, represented France at youth level.

He was named player of the tournament when the French side won the European Under-19 Championship in 2010.



In 2017 Kakuta switched allegiance to DR Congo, the homeland of his parents, and has scored five goals in 31 appearances.

He is yet to make it on to the pitch at this World Cup. But perhaps the strange, rather sad story of Kakuta and English football will have one more twist.

Sports.title: Jermaine Jenas and new girlfriend Anne Leplaideur look tense on holiday in Ibiza – weeks after going public with romance
Sports.content:
JERMAINE Jenas and his new girlfriend Anne Leplaideur have been seen looking tense while on holiday in Ibiza.

The couple went public with their romance last month after reportedly meeting last year.





But they didn’t appear to be looking too happy while being spotted on the Spanish island.

They were pictured on a stroll as both of them failed to crack a smile and walked side by side.

Jermaine, 43, appeared straight-faced as he donned a white t-shirt and navy shorts.

He wore a cap on his head and a pair of clogs as well as a gold chain around his neck.



Meanwhile, Anne, 31, opted for a white cover-up over her bikini along with matching sandals.

She accessorised with a black handbag over her shoulder and some black sunglasses.

The pair were not holding hands and appeared to look quite tense while on their walk.

The Sun exclusively revealed the two were dating last month.

A source confirmed at the time: “Jermaine has been dating Anne since December.



“He has tried to keep a low profile with their relationship.

“His circle just know he’s dating a woman who works in Paris in properties.

“At the start he would drop hints on social media — like posts of Anne’s Chanel handbag when they were on dates. But now he’s in Paris so much it is clear it’s serious.



“Jermaine is always posting pictures from Paris and says he’s happier than ever.

“Anne has been to visit him in London too but because his work schedule is less regimented now, he can spend more time in France.

“You only have to look at the size of his smile to see he’s smitten with Anne.”

The presenter split from his wife Ellie Penfold last year after 16 years together.

They had tied the knot back in 2011 and share three children together.



It came just months after he was sacked by the BBC over “inappropriate texts” sent to female colleagues.

He revealed she was raging once his indiscretions were revealed and had raging rows but told The Sun they had moved past it with the help of couples therapy.

The former pro-footballer appeared on Good Morning Britain earlier this month as he clashed with hosts Ranvir Singh and Kate Garraway as they quizzed him over his sexting scandal.



The former One Show host was pressed on the topic by Ranvir, who accused him of “skirting round the question”.

She said: “What is your advice to other men then? I find this really interesting because you’re skirting around what you’ve learnt.

Jenas snapped back at the GMB host, saying: “I’m not skirting around anything, Ranvir.

He later accused Kate of asking an “unfair question” when she quizzed him on what he had learnt from his sacking.

Sports.title: Extreme weather warning for England training camp as 'heatdome' to engulf World Cup
Sports.content:
Extreme weather warning for England training camp as 'heatdome' to engulf World Cup

England's World Cup base in Kansas City is set to be hit by a dangerous heatwave with temperatures on the rise as they gear up to face DR Congo on Wednesday in the round of 32

View 3 Images England's stars such as Trevoh Chalobah (pictured) will need to stay hydrated and cool

England's World Cup training camp in Kansas City is set to be hit by a 'heatdome' ahead of their round of 32 clash with DR Congo in Atlanta. Thomas Tuchel's men have made a point of adapting to the hot and humid climate in North America throughout the tournament, but a roasting heatwave is poised to hit Missouri in the coming days until Friday night that will make conditions almost unbearable.

‌



A threatening heat dome will engulf the central and eastern parts of America this week with heat index temperatures - a combination of air temperature with humidity - soaring into the triple-digits in some areas. Heat index values are expected to reach figures as high as 43.3 degrees celsius (110 degrees Fahrenheit) ahead of the knockout clash.

‌



Host cities such as Boston, Philadelphia and Kansas City are all expected to be heavily affected by the sweltering temperatures, which raises even more concerns as their respective stadiums are all open-air venues with very little cover.

‌



“This week is going to be very, very hot,” said Geoff Cornish, assistant chief video meteorologist for the weather forecasting company AccuWeather. “This is going be a significant heatwave, the likes of which we don’t see in every single year.”

The National Weather Service issued an extreme heat watch for Philadelphia and other East Coast regions starting on Wednesday afternoon heading all the way up to Saturday evening. Warnings suggest temperatures could reach 'feels-like' levels of up to 110 F (43.3 C) during the daytime, forcing FIFA to amend the opening hours of the Fan Festival in Philadelphia.

England's World Cup round of 32 fear as Thomas Tuchel braced for repeat READ MORE :

England superfan travelled over 17 hours on three buses to get to next World Cup game READ MORE :

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



The New York City area could also see near-record high temperatures of nearly 43 degrees celsius, with little respite overnight. An extreme heat watch will be in effect from Wednesday afternoon to Saturday evening. The heat index in Boston and much of southern New England could skyrocket to 44C, with the weather warning starting Wednesday morning.

“This level of heat can be deadly for those without adequate cooling and hydration,” the National Weather Service said, adding that it could also impact transportation and electrical and water systems.

FIFA's three-minute hydration breaks, which occur once every 23 minutes during the game, have been controversial due to their use for advert breaks. However, in these conditions, players and staff will need every bit of water and time in the shade to protect from the hot weather.

‌



View 3 Images England have been training in Kansas City, Missouri (Image: CHANDAN KHANNA, AFP via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

There are concerns that the heat could trigger exertional heat illness, which is when the human body’s temperature gets too hot and is accompanied by significant strain from intense exercise on a sizzling day. Symptoms include extreme fatigue, impaired performance, headaches, irritability, nausea, dizziness, cramping and dehydration.

‌



Prior to the World Cup, Tuchel admitted that his players would struggle to cope with the soaring temperatures and dense humidity in North America after a draining season. However, the German added he would be prepared for the eventuality.

"The conditions are not our biggest enemy but it is not to our advantage after a long and very demanding season for our players," Tuchel said earlier in June.

‌



"We are not used to being in this kind of heat and humidity, and even altitude if we play in Mexico. There will be a lot of challenges in this World Cup. The heat is one of them but we are prepared already."

It's an issue Tuchel has taken seriously and as he stated, meticulously prepared for. In June 2025, the German coach instructed his squad to take specially-devised digital capsules during a warm-weather training camp to measure their internal temperature and record how quickly they were able to cool down.

View 3 Images England manager Thomas Tuchel has prepared for the heat

‌



Players also trained in specially-heated tents to replicate the conditions at the tournament: "We know the individual reaction of the players to the heat and we have cooling strategies in place," Tuchel said.

"We've had help from Team GB and specialists all over the world to come up with solutions that help the players to adapt. We know exactly the amount of time we want to expose them in pre-camp, the ideal amount of time that you should train in the sun and that we also don't do too much."

For spectators, volunteers and workers, the greatest dangers could be outside the stadiums in fan zones, transportation routes, car parks and outdoor celebrations. Fans guzzling beer and other alcohol could also be at risk due to its dehydrating qualities.

Sports.title: World Cup LIVE: Germany and Netherlands out on penalties as VAR 'scandal' leaves team stunned
Sports.content:
Paraguay's players celebrate celebrate after winning the penalty shootout during the 2026 World Cup round of 32 football match between Germany and Paraguay at the Boston Stadium in Foxborough on June 29, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

Brazil and Paraguay have become the next two teams to join Canada in the Round of 16 after both secured their passage through on Monday, leaving Japan and Germany OUT

Germany and Netherlands have both been knocked out of the World Cup following shock Round of 32 defeats to Paraguay and Morocco respectively.

Julian Nagelsmann's side went into the tie as strong favourites to progress to the last 16 after topping Group E and facing a Paraguay side who scraped through as the seventh best third place team in the tournament.

But football doesn't seem to work like that, as Paraguay stunned their opponents to win on penalties following a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Julio Enciso, the former Brighton midfielder, opened the scoring for Paraguay in the first half before Arsenal's Kai Havertz levelled after the break.

Although the South American missed two opportunities to win the shootout, they still kept their nerve to run out 4-3 winners on spot-kicks and secure a place in the Round of 16 against either France or Sweden.

Netherlands, meanwhile, missed three of their spot-kicks with Justin Kluivert, Quinten Timber and Crysencio Summerville the unfortunate trio, as Morocco keeper Bono made himself a hero once again by saving the West Ham attacker's spot-kick.

Elsewhere, Brazil sealed a spot in the next round earlier on Monday after coming from behind and scoring a dramatic stoppage-time winner to beat Japan. Kaishu Sano had put the Samurai Blue in front on the half hour mark, but Brazil turned it around in the second half with Casemiro equalising before Arsenal's Gabriel Martinelli was the man of the moment, netting in the 95th minute to make it 2-1.

The knockout stage continues today as Norway take on the Ivory Coast, France face Sweden and Mexico face Ecuador at home.

Sports.title: Riot police charge as fans hit by water cannon after Netherlands vs Morocco penalty shootout
Sports.content:
Riot police charge as fans hit by water cannon after Netherlands vs Morocco penalty shootout

Police had to intervene in celebrations across the Netherlands after Morocco defeat Oranje in a dramatic World Cup penalty shootout and see jubilant scenes

View 2 Images Riot police and water cannons were used in Hague (Image: Ongehoord Nederland TV/X)

Water cannons were used on fans as riot police were forced to intervene in the Netherlands following the nation's World Cup exit to Morocco. The country's Moroccan population launched into jubilant celebrations in the early hours of Tuesday morning, after their side earned a dramatic penalty shootout victory over the Netherlands.

‌



High-profile players such as Noussair Mazraoui, Sofyan Amrabat, and Anass Salah-Eddine were all born in the Netherlands before choosing to represent Morocco, as Hakim Ziyech had done in the past, adding another layer of rivalry between the countries. A 400,000-strong community of Moroccans live in the Netherlands.

‌



Car horns and fireworks were heard across the country's major cities, including Amsterdam and Utrecht, but the happy scenes were marred by some unsavoury actions. In Hague, a large police presence was deployed in the Schilderswijk district ahead of the match.

‌



Local authorities reported that police officers were 'pelted with fireworks and stones' before riot police charged and a water cannon was deployed as arrests were made. It was described as a 'cat-and-mouse game' between fans and the police as the latter attempted to clear the area.

As cars attempted to pass through the area, it was claimed that one was attacked with someone jumping on the vehicle's roof before the driver quickly got away.

Cristiano Ronaldo consoles Chelsea legend after father's death as World Cup exit confirmed READ MORE :

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



De Telegraaf reported that police were forced to intervene in Utrecht as 'hooded individuals' knocked over safety barriers. They claimed that it was a 'dangerous situation' for commuters before troublemakers were dispersed.

It was also said to be 'chaos' in Amsterdam, while Rotterdam's West-Kruiskade neighbourhood had to be evacuated after more than two hours of celebrations. Celebrations were permitted for a long time before police decided to end the festivities.

Police made announcements over a megaphone on multiple occasions before the arrest unit was deployed. In all locations, normality appeared to be restored by 8.30am.

‌



View 2 Images Noussair Mazraoui celebrates the victory (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

Cody Gakpo looked to have secured victory for the Netherlands before Issa Diop secured a 91st-minute equaliser. The Dutch side then failed to be clinical in the penalty shootout as Justin Kluivert, Quinten Timber and Crysencio Summerville all missed from the spot to crash out of the World Cup.

Head coach Ronald Koeman has come in for criticism following his side's exit. "This defeat is Koeman's fault, because I didn't recognise this Dutch team," Zlatan Ibrahimovic said on FOX Sports.

‌



"He lost with an identity that is not the Dutch identity. That makes me angry. I was always taught: attack, attack, attack. This is not the Dutch identity.

"Today, Koeman looked like an Italian coach playing not to lose, whereas the Netherlands always plays to win. If you lose, at least lose with your own identity and don't change it.

"This was not the Netherlands I am used to seeing. You can also tell by the way they played that they didn't feel comfortable. The possession was gone, the attacking football was gone...It just looked very bad, and that was all Koeman's fault. I thought it was absolutely nothing, really nothing at all."

Sports.title: Liverpool learn where they stand with PSG's Bradley Barcola stance after Yan Diomande move
Sports.content:
Liverpool learn where they stand with PSG's Bradley Barcola stance after Yan Diomande move

Liverpool have been credited with an interest in signing Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola, having appeared to miss out on Yan Diomande to the French giants

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked with Liverpool this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Liverpool have been handed a potentially significant blow to their hopes of landing Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola.

‌



The Reds have repeatedly been linked with a move for the France international during the summer transfer window.

‌



Andoni Iraola will be hard at work preparing for his debut season as Liverpool's new manager following confirmation of his appointment earlier this month, taking over from Arne Slot in the hotseat.

‌



Barcola has been linked with Liverpool for quite some time, and speculation surrounding a potential transfer intensified following the recent news regarding Diomande's preference to move to Paris.

A report in The Athletic has suggested, however, that PSG have no intention of selling Barcola, and have slapped a price tag on the 23-year-old of more than £116million - the same figure that Manchester City are reportedly set to pay to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic gives brutal Ronald Koeman verdict after Netherlands World Cup exit READ MORE :

Barcola is contracted to PSG until the summer of 2028, and the report suggests he is not currently prepared to put pen to paper on fresh terms.

‌



Despite this, PSG appear firmly intent on keeping Barcola at the Parc des Princes this summer, which could represent a considerable setback for Liverpool as they seek to strengthen their wide forward options.

Liverpool have long been anticipated to conduct significant transfer business this summer, especially following the exits of Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate, all of whom departed as free agents.

RB Leipzig starlet Yan Diomande has emerged as a primary target for Liverpool this summer, with the Reds already indicating a readiness to offer up to £86million for the Ivory Coast international.

‌

Yet reports over the weekend suggested that Diomande had indicated a desire to join PSG, with the Champions League winners now appearing as frontrunners to land the gifted 19-year-old.

An earlier report from The Athletic indicated that Liverpool had pinpointed alternatives to Diomande should a move for the Ivory Coast international fail to materialise.

Brighton's Yankuba Minteh, FC Koln's Said El Mala and Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo have all been mentioned as possible alternatives to Diomande for Liverpool, though there has been no significant development regarding any of the three.

Sports.title: Premier League title winner heads for Dubai to team up with Jonjo Shelvey and Ravel Morrison
Sports.content:
Premier League title winner heads for Dubai to team up with Jonjo Shelvey and Ravel Morrison

Danny Simpson has come out of retirement to join UAE Second Division side Arabian Falcons as a player-coach, where he will also link up with former Manchester United star Ravel Morrison

View 3 Images Danny Simpson has come out of retirement from professional football (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United academy star and Leicester City defender Danny Simpson has ended his retirement to sign for a Dubai-based club as a player-coach. Simpson has linked up with Arabian Falcons, who compete in the UAE Second Division, where he will also reunite with former United star Ravel Morrison, the club's current captain.

‌



Simpson, 39, spent five years as a United first-team player after joining the squad in 2005, before eventually leaving Old Trafford in 2010 to seal a permanent switch to Newcastle.

‌



The former right-back went on to claim a Premier League title winners' medal with Leicester in 2016, and announced his retirement from professional football in the summer of 2024. He also had stints at Huddersfield, Bristol City and Macclesfield before calling time on his playing career.

‌



Now, however, Simpson is back in the game and has headed to Dubai, where he will work alongside former Liverpool midfielder Jonjo Shelvey, who takes charge as the club's manager.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Zlatan Ibrahimovic gives brutal Ronald Koeman verdict after Netherlands World Cup exit READ MORE :

Former Crystal Palace midfielder Jason Puncheon is also a co-owner of Arabian Falcons and serves as head of football operations.

‌



Opening up about his decision, Simpson has explained what persuaded him to come out of retirement and head to the UAE.

“The opportunity to join Jonjo and this exciting project was one I couldn’t turn down,” Simpson said. “I still have plenty to offer on the pitch, and I’m looking forward to helping the team achieve its ambitions.

3 View 3 Images Jonjo Shelvey has retired and is managing UAE third-tier club Arabian Falcons (Image: Arabian Falcons) 3 View 3 Images Ravel Morrison was a potential world beater, but became a journeyman footballer

‌



“The club has a clear plan, and I want to play my part in delivering a successful promotion-winning campaign.”

Shelvey has also expressed his delight at bringing Simpson to the club. He said: “I’m really pleased to welcome Danny Simpson to Arabian Falcons. After stepping in for the last five games last season and coming so close to promotion, we now have the opportunity to build properly in my first full campaign.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



“Danny is the ideal signing - a Premier League champion with vast experience, leadership, and a winning mentality.

“He strengthens us immediately on the pitch and will be invaluable in helping develop the squad. This is the start of us building a team I firmly believe can win promotion this season.”

Puncheon also outlined what he believes Simpson will contribute to the club, while making clear the Arabian Falcons' ambitions for the season ahead.

‌



“This signing sends a strong message about our ambition,” Puncheon said. “Jonjo has already shown what he can do in a short space of time, and with Danny arriving we are building real strength and character in the squad.

“We are fully focused on making this a successful season and securing promotion to the UAE First Division.”

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford could now STAY at Man Utd after showdown talks with club bosses
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford could now STAY at Man Utd after showdown talks with club bosses

Marcus Rashford is set to return to Manchester United for pre-season after the World Cup with positive talks held between the club and the player's camp over his future

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could stick with Manchester United this summer (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford could be offered an opportunity to salvage his Manchester United career following constructive discussions between the club and the player's representatives.

‌



Rashford is currently at the World Cup with England but is expected to return to Carrington for pre-season in the coming weeks with his long-term future still unclear after spending last season on loan with Barcelona.

‌



The 28 year old will link up with the first-team squad when he does arrive for training and will be in contention for selection during pre-season under Michael Carrick, meaning he could appear in some of the six friendlies United will contest before the new Premier League season.

‌



It had been assumed that Rashford would depart Old Trafford for good in the transfer window, even after Barcelona opted against exercising the clause to sign him permanently for £26million and instead pursued a £69m deal for his England colleague, Anthony Gordon.

Eight Man Utd rules Michael Carrick has scrapped including dressing room ban READ MORE :

Now, though, there is a sense that Rashford could stay at United past the close of the transfer window after discussions between both parties established the foundation for his return in pre-season. And there is now a readiness on all sides to explore a reintegration for Rashford, per the Manchester Evening News.

That outcome is far from certain, and a late window offer could yet alter the picture, but United are currently unwilling to sanction a third loan spell after Rashford's stints at Aston Villa and Barcelona. Rashford had been keen to prolong his time in Catalonia, but United are reluctant to enter fresh negotiations with the La Liga outfit.

‌



Premier League clubs are expected to circle for Rashford this summer, though he would sooner run down the final two years of his contract than commit to a permanent switch to another top-flight side at this point.

View 2 Images Barcelona paid big money to sign Anthony Gordon before the World Cup despite holding an option to make Rashford's stay at the Nou Camp permanent (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

That has left the door ajar for a return to United, and it had already been settled that Rashford would feature in the first-team setup this summer, having been ostracised into the 'bomb squad' by Ruben Amorim 12 months ago.

‌



United are keen to bolster their left flank this summer and have cast their eye over Everton's Iliman Ndiaye and West Ham's Crysencio Summerville as possible targets, though those pursuits could be abandoned should Rashford remain at Old Trafford.

He could battle it out with Matheus Cunha and Patrick Dorgu on the left and would also provide cover for Benjamin Sesko through the middle.

Should Rashford be brought back into the fold, United could redirect funds set aside for a wide left signing towards further midfield reinforcement, with Manuel Ugarte now set to miss most of next season through a serious knee injury.

‌



For the time being, United press on with their pursuit of West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes, having already wrapped up the signing of Ederson from Atalanta.

Sports.title: 'It's been a difficult period’ – Newey speaks on health issues
Sports.content:
Aston Martin team principal Adrian Newey has said he is doing “ok now” after going through a “difficult period” with health issues.

The legendary F1 designer was speaking in a wide-ranging interview with Aston Martin's website ahead of their home British Grand Prix this weekend in which he also addressed the team's humbling start to the sport's new era of rules and confirmed plans to introduce a first big car upgrade in Hungary at the end of July.

On his spell of ill health, Newey said: "I'm ok now, but it's been a difficult period.

"I said earlier [about the team's start to the season], it never rains but it pours.

"In truth, I was not 100 per cent last year. I had to balance health and work much more carefully.

"The team handled it incredibly well.

"I kept a very good relationship with the engineers and I don't feel it caused too much of a blip. That's a testament to how adaptable and supportive everyone here is."

Hungarian GP car overhaul confirmed

On the track, Aston Martin have endured a wretched start to the 2026 season.

The outfit have regularly been the slowest car in the field despite entering F1's new rules era with what appeared the dream ticket of a first car designed by Newey - whose challengers have won 25 world titles across three different decades - and a works engine deal with Honda, winners of recent championships with Red Bull.

Newey admits the team "probably put too much expectation on ourselves" for the start of 2026 and that delays in starting the design of the all-new car last year, and the Silverstone-based outfit not yet being operationally strong enough, had contributed to the problems.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Adrian Newey breaks down how the vibration and battery issues are impacting Aston Martin after the first day on track at Melbourne

Honda have also experienced vibration and reliability issues with their underperforming power unit.

Aston Martin have scored a solitary point in eight grands prix so far with their short-term struggles increased by what Newey admits was the "painful decision" to not bring regular small updates to the AMR26 like the rest of the grid on a race-by-race basis until one bigger overhaul was ready.

But Newey is convinced that approach will prove to be in the team's best long-term interests, with that first upgrade now confirmed for the Hungarian Grand Prix on July 24-26.

"We plan to introduce our upgrade in Hungary on both cars," said Newey.

"The main structural elements remain the same - the chassis and gearbox architecture don't fundamentally change - but we've taken weight out of both, which required re-homologating and crash testing the forward chassis.

"The front suspension is unchanged. The rear suspension is slightly revised.

"We've developed a new nose and substantially revised aerodynamic surfaces. So, while the core structure is similar, it's a big aerodynamic package coupled with significant weight reduction. The target is to get very close to the weight limit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso hits the wall at the during the first practice session to bring out the red flag at the Monaco GP

Newey, who added the title of team principal at the start of the year to his existing role of managing technical partner, is expecting a sizeable improvement in lap time but is remaining cautious on the absolute outcome.

"We're predicting a large step, but I'm reluctant to put specific numbers out there because our simulation tools aren't yet as sophisticated or well correlated as they need to be," added the 67-year-old

"Historically, at this team, there hasn't been enough investment in engineering simulation tools - not just project management systems, but the core physics tools themselves. We're putting that investment in now, but you don't rewrite and validate those tools overnight. Correlating them properly with the real car takes time.

"At the moment, they're improving, but the real gains from that work will come later in the year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso seemed to suggest this will be the last time he will ever race at the Barcelona-Catalunya circuit with the race off the calendar until 2028

Will Alonso stay for 2027?

On the future of star driver Fernando Alonso, whose contract at the team ends after this season, Newey is optimistic that if they can show the 44-year-old "clear, tangible progress" with their Hungary upgrade then he will stay for 2027.

Asked how important the Budapest upgrade was for Alonso, who is set to weigh up his F1 future this summer, Newey said: "It's very important. Fernando is really looking forward to the upgrade and, if it performs, we hope he'll be in the cockpit for another season.

"Given his experience, his feel for the car, his ability to guide development, he's a tremendous asset.

"But he wants to see clear, tangible progress. If we can show that we're moving decisively in the right direction, he's absolutely committed to being behind the wheel."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix

Newey says the whole team are motivated to get themselves back up the grid.

"You walk around the AMR Technology Campus at night and the lights are still on. There are a lot of late evenings, a lot of motivation, and a real determination to prove that we can do this," he added.

"We have the facilities, we have the people, we have huge amounts of talent. The task is to make it all gel - and to an extent, take the pressure off ourselves so we can breathe and concentrate on medium‑ and long‑term projects, not just the next race.

"That means not only solving our immediate aero and mechanical issues, but also introducing better systems and processes that underpin how we design and build the car."

Sports.title: Merson: Bellingham's deeper role has given Tuchel midfield headache
Sports.content:
Paul Merson thinks England boss Thomas Tuchel has a bit of a midfield headache after Jude Bellingham's excellent performance in a deeper role in the 2-0 win over Panama.

Bellingham lined up alongside Elliot Anderson and grabbed a goal and an assist in an all-action midfield display, leaving Tuchel with plenty to think about ahead of the Three Lions' last 32 clash with DR Congo on Wednesday.

But with Declan Rice expected to come back into England's starting XI, Merson believes Tuchel has a dilemma over how he constructs his midfield as the knockout stages get under way.

Read on for former England international Merson's thoughts in full...

Will Tuchel keep Bellingham in a deeper role?

Image: Bellingham in action for England against Panama

Thomas Tuchel now has a major problem after Jude Bellingham's performance in a deeper role against Panama.

Bellingham really impressed for me, but that is where Declan Rice plays and if fit, he plays.

But the plus for England having Bellingham in that role is that it is so much harder for the opposition to pick him up when he's coming from deeper.

Morgan Rogers really struggled in the No 10 role. He hardly touched the ball, just like Bellingham struggled to have an impact against Ghana, who also sat deep to defend.

It's just so congested in that area of the pitch, but as a deeper midfielder you can make runs past the opposition easier and it is so much harder for them to pick up.

Image: Bellingham ranks first among England players across a raft of key metrics

So what does Tuchel do? Rice plays. There is no doubt about that for me.

You have to look at the all-round picture. No disrespect to Panama, but when we come up against the bigger teams, you'll need Rice.

Could you pair Bellingham with Rice? That might be tough on Elliot Anderson, but I think the problem then is what do you do in the No 10 position? Rogers didn't exactly have the game of his life against Panama, but Bellingham also wasn't at his best against Ghana.

We need to address how we are going to get the ball into whoever plays in the No 10 position so that they can impact the game.

'England have got to work out how to get the ball into Bellingham'

Image: Jude Bellingham starred in a deeper role for England against Panama

I wasn't surprised by Bellingham's performance in that deeper role.

He's a top player. He wants to be on the ball, and he wants to be involved in everything. He plays the game like an enthusiastic school kid.

It reminds me of Wayne Rooney. They want the ball, and they want to have an impact all over the pitch.

Bellingham has got more chance of getting the ball in the position he played against Panama rather than the one he played against Ghana.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News reporter Rob Dorsett reflects on England's 2-0 win over Panama at the World Cup

The key for England is trying to get whoever is playing in the No 8 and No 10 positions on the ball.

Against Ghana, Bellingham was showing all the time but no-one was getting him the ball.

I'm not comparing Bellingham to Lionel Messi, but if you watch Messi, Argentina give him the ball whenever they can. They pass to him in tight spaces and Bellingham is not afraid to do the same, but England need to build the confidence to be able to give it to him whenever they can.

It's going to be tricky for Bellingham to back to the No 10 position, if that is what Tuchel decides to do. DR Congo are going to sit deep, too, with 10 behind the ball.

'England don't have to have hit their peak yet'

Image: Harry Kane and Bellingham scored as England finally shook off Panama to top their World Cup group

Every time the England players are getting on the ball they have two or even three defenders around them.

We are moving the ball quickly to get it out to the wide players but they are doubled up on every time.

Marcus Rashford had the ball a lot in the first half against Panama but didn't really do much. We were all calling for him to start ahead of Anthony Gordon but there was no end product.

Bukayo Saka looks as if he is struggling a little, but I think he has to play.

He might be carrying a little niggle, we don't really know, but I just can't see a world where Saka is not starting for England in the big games as we progress in this tournament.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol says Harry Kane should be a contender for the coveted Ballon d'Or after becoming England's greatest World Cup goalscorer on top of an impressive season with Bayern Munich

This is where the tournament starts really. You don't have to have hit your peak yet.

I like the fact England aren't relying on just one player in this tournament. Harry Kane has got his goals, the defence was okay against Ghana and Jude Bellingham stepped up against Panama.

That's what you need. We cannot just keep waiting on Kane to deliver.

We have four wingers in the squad and I think it's a good thing that none of them have really got going. They are yet to really get going but if that can change as we reach and go into the knockout rounds, that can only be a positive for Tuchel.

The wingers have been a six out of 10 so far, so if they can get themselves up a few marks England will have a good chance of going quite far. They may just be the match winners as we develop into this tournament.

'England will have to get better but they have World Cup chance'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel reflects on England's 2-0 win over Panama, which sealed their place in the knockout stages of the World Cup as group winners

England will have to get better.

There is something in improving when you are playing against better teams, but the concern is you just can't turn it on and off like a tap.

You have to keep building and get better match by match. That's what I want to see now, starting against DR Congo.

I think they've been a seven out of 10 so far from what I saw in the group stage. We did what we needed to do against Croatia, Ghana and Panama. We'll need more but it's a good start.

France going forward are phenomenal, Spain are Spain but I don't think they will blow you away. They leave you in the game. I really liked Colombia when I watched them against Portugal. They played with a lot of pace and energy and they know the conditions well.

It's a very open World Cup, in my opinion. A lot of teams have players that can hurt you on any given day. If you have a good day, you have a chance, and that's what I love about the World Cup.

Whatever happens, you've got to beat some really good teams to win.

There's a lot still to play for in terms of England. Yes, we've had the reality checks against Ghana and - I also think - against Panama. That's a worry.

But while we are in this tournament, we have a chance to win it. Now's the time to reproduce what we saw against Croatia - and if we do, we have a chance. It's the hope that really does get to you.

Sports.title: Wilder next for Usyk? 'Fury chapter is closed'
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk has chosen to end his world title reign, but will fight once more before his expected retirement from the sport.

His team have essentially ruled out a trilogy fight with Tyson Fury before the end of his career.

Sergey Lapin, the CEO of Usyk's promotional company Ready To Fight, told Sky Sports: "I don't really see much point in it. Oleksandr has already beaten Tyson Fury twice and answered every question inside the ring.

"I believe that chapter is closed, and today that fight no longer carries the same level of interest."

Usyk's final world title fight was against kickboxing star Rico Verhoeven. Although Usyk's late stoppage victory has prompted much debate a potential rematch with Verhoeven is considered unlikely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oleksandr Usyk survived an incredible performance from kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven as the fight was waved off with seconds remaining in the eleventh round. Highlights courtesy of DAZN and Ring Magazine

"It's possible. But honestly, I'm not sure it's the fight that fans are looking for today," Lapin said.

Usyk has previously expressed an interest in fighting Deontay Wilder, the high profile former world champion from Alabama. A contest with Usyk is something Wilder has targeted, too.

Zuffa Boxing could be open to staging Usyk vs Wilder, with promoter Dana White hinting: "Anything is possible."

Usyk-Wilder would most likely be held in America, though Usyk does still harbour a dream of boxing one last time in his Ukrainian homeland. That has been impossible for the former Olympic and undisputed champion since Russia launched its full scale invasion of Ukraine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dana White did not dismiss suggestions that Oleksandr Usyk's farewell fight against Deontay Wilder could be promoted by Zuffa

"Saudi Arabia and the United States are both outstanding venues for major events. But if we're talking about a dream, it would undoubtedly be Ukraine," Lapin said.

Established now as a boxing great, Usyk has won every major title in the sport, amateur and professional. He is planning for a future beyond the ropes.

"Family will always come first for Oleksandr. After his career, he wants to spend more time with his loved ones, continue helping Ukraine, contribute to the development of sport in his country, and create opportunities for the next generation of Ukrainian athletes," Lapin said.

"That mission is just as important to him as everything he achieved inside the ring."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Andy Scott is joined by Hamzah Sheeraz and Tony Sims as they discuss Oleksandr Usyk's much-talked-about stoppage victory over Rico Verhoeven

Wilder on Usyk

Previously Deontay Wilder told Sky Sports why he wanted to fight Usyk: "He's one of the best in the era. I do need him to accomplish what I need to accomplish.

"It can happen and it will happen. As long as I have the confidence to do what I have to do, it will happen.

"I must accomplish what I set forth in the beginning of my career."

Sports.title: Why Tuchel should be worried about DR Congo's 'anti-England' formula
Sports.content:
If you're looking for a dark horse in the knockout stages, don't look for one in DR Congo. Look for a Leopard - patient, relentless, and ready to pounce when it matters most.

Portugal came away licking their wounds, with weaknesses exposed in their meeting with DR Congo.

While Cristiano Ronaldo was shackled by a combination of captain Chancel Mbemba and Burnley's Axel Tuanzebe at the back, Joao Neves' sixth-minute header was Portugal's only shot on target throughout the game.

Not only did DR Congo earn a point against Portugal, who entered the competition as one of the pre-tournament favourites, but many observers would be justified in arguing that Sebastien Desabre's side deserved to leave with all three points after an impressive display. Yoane Wissa's headed goal came in a brave DR Congo performance.

Colombia posed a different kind of test, and although DR Congo eventually succumbed to late pressure, their identity was unmistakable: defend first, ask questions later. DR Congo's defence appeared more vulnerable in Guadalajara, but they could rely on an inspired Lionel Mpasi goalkeeping display to keep Colombia's heavy hitters at bay.

Victory over Uzbekistan marked the greatest moment in DR Congo's footballing history, propelling the Leopards into uncharted territory.

In the nation's first-ever taste of knockout football at the World Cup, England represent a free-hit for the Leopards that they will be keen to take.

Familiar faces in the DR Congo squad Aaron Wan- Bissaka , West Ham

, West Ham Axel Tuanzebe , Burnley

, Burnley Arthur Masuaku , Lens (ex-West Ham & Sunderland)

, Lens (ex-West Ham & Sunderland) Chancel Mbemba , Lille (ex-Newcastle)

, Lille (ex-Newcastle) Noah Sadiki , Sunderland

, Sunderland Edo Kayembe , Watford

, Watford Gael Kakuta , AE Larissa (ex-Chelsea)

, AE Larissa (ex-Chelsea) Yoane Wissa , Newcastle

, Newcastle Aaron Tshibola, Kilmarnock (ex-Aston Villa & Nott'm Forest)

Why Congo's style could trouble England

DR Congo are not a side designed to entertain; they are a nation built to avoid losing and biding their time. The defence is where Desabre has placed his focus during his reign.

Under his four-year stewardship, DR Congo have never been beaten by more than one goal. For context, Thomas Tuchel, who took charge of England last year, has already suffered a two-goal defeat, losing 3-1 to Senegal.

DR Congo find success during low-scoring games with Desabre's side scoring one goal or fewer in two-thirds of their matches.

In the opening two games, against Portugal and Colombia, Desabre set his side up with a back five, three workmen in the middle and a front two. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Arthur Masuaku, deployed as wing-backs, were more disciplined than adventurous. Despite providing the team's width, the creative responsibility largely fell to the midfield.

DR Congo are more than happy to surrender possession, inviting opponents onto their resolute defensive block before striking when the opportunity arises.

The inquest into England's lack of creativity, inspiration or energy in attacking areas continues despite their 2-0 win over Panama. According to FIFA's style metrics, England are one of just four teams whose playing style differs most from that of DR Congo.

The blueprint has already been laid by Ghana, and it's one that Desabre and Congo are well-versed in. As the game progressed against the Ghanaians, England's lack of penetration offered hope to the Black Stars, who couldn't make use of their moments on the counterattack.

On a quest to fix that, don't expect Tuchel to find easy prey to remedy that against the stubborn DR Congo.

Don't underestimate Congo's attack

Image: Yoane Wissa has scored three goals at the World Cup

DR Congo's conservative style doesn't take away from their threat in attack, though.

Wissa has three goals in the competition so far, matching Harry Kane's tally and more than Ronaldo's return. After finding the net in the curtain-raiser, Wissa struck twice against Uzbekistan to take his tally to three goals in three games - already surpassing his Newcastle output threefold after his £55m move to the Magpies.

In truth, Wissa's involvement after missing the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) as part of a good gesture to Newcastle has been more than welcome.

Alongside the 29-year-old, Desabre has opted to play Real Betis striker Cedric Bakambu, who is yet to register a shot on target at the World Cup, as his personal goalscoring issues continue.

Against Uzbekistan, Desabre added a new dimension to the attack with Fiston Mayele when he replaced Bakambu. Earlier this season, the Pyramids forward was named the men's Interclub African Player of the Year.

The award recognises the best African player who plays their football within the continent. He added something that Bakambu couldn't provide, which was composure in front of goal, necessary in a game of few chances.

Desabre's adaptability had been questioned in the build-up to DR Congo's match against Uzbekistan. However, a switch to a flat back four and the introduction of Nathan Mbuku and Brian Cipenga, two wingers, paid off.

The pair will be eager to start once again, but both have proved they can potentially provide an impact from the bench.

Why Congo's clash against England means more

Though the two nations have never met in a competitive capacity, in a footballing sense, both DR Congo and England have strong links.

Those mainly come from a community of young players who earn their stripes playing in England. Tuanzebe was born in Bunia, Congo, but moved to Rochdale at a very young age.

He would then find a footballing education at Manchester United and even wear the captain's armband on one occasion. Tuanzebe also represented England at youth level, sharing an international dressing room with the likes of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Dominic Solanke.

Image: Aaron Wan-Bissaka was born in Croydon, while Axel Tuanzebe grew up in Rochdale

Wan-Bissaka, who also played at United, was born and raised in south London before making the switch to Old Trafford.

The right-back went as far as being included in a Gareth Southgate England squad back in 2019. Midfielder Aaron Tshibola, formerly of Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest and now of Kilmarnock, was born in east London.

Meanwhile, Arthur Masuaku is a name England fans will also recognise for spells at West Ham and Sunderland, while current Black Cats star Noah Sadiki is a highly rated member of the team.

There's even DR Congo heritage within the England squad in Ezri Konsa, who would be eligible to represent the Leopards.

Alongside the personal stories, after a 52-year wait for a World Cup, Wednesday's clash will be a furthering of the history that is already being made. The England match marks DR Congo's most successful period in a generation.

Eyes, all of a sudden, will be on DR Congo, who have been a sleeping giant for African football for over a century. When DR Congo, previously called Zaire, participated at the 1974 World Cup, they were the first sub-Saharan African country to qualify.

The chance to showcase that against England is one the entire nation will embrace, hoping the players wearing its colours rise to the occasion in the same way. DR Congo is back on the map.
